title: Fisher's fundamental theorem of natural selection (partial-change form)

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Fisher's fundamental theorem of natural selection (partial-change form)

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: The rate of increase in mean fitness of a population due to natural selection equals its additive genetic variance in fitness at that time.

fields.label: Notation
fields.value: \Delta_{NS}\bar{w} = V_A(w)/\bar{w} (discrete generations); \left.\frac{d\bar{m}}{dt}\right|_{NS} = V_A(m) for Malthusian fitness m

fields.label: Work
fields.value: The Genetical Theory of Natural Selection

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: The Genetical Theory of Natural Selection (1930)

fields.label: Source as written
fields.value: Ronald A. Fisher (1930) The Genetical Theory of Natural Selection

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: Cursor agent (Claude Opus 5.5) extracting key claims from source papers

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: the 'partial change' holds average effects of alleles and the environment fixed (Price 1972, Ewens 1989); V_A is the additive genetic variance in fitness

fields.label: Formal status in the nanopub
fields.value: proved in this partial-change reading. Read as a claim about the total change in mean fitness it is false under dominance, epistasis, frequency dependence or a changing environment.

fields.label: Notation
fields.value: \Delta_{NS}\bar{w} = V_A(w)/\bar{w} (discrete generations); \left.\frac{d\bar{m}}{dt}\right|_{NS} = V_A(m) for Malthusian fitness m

fields.label: Proposed test
fields.value: In a pedigreed wild population or an experimental-evolution line, estimate the additive genetic variance in relative fitness (animal model) and compare it with the observed per-generation response of breeding values for fitness, separating the selection term from environmental deterioration.
